paper.paper_scope: Examines the strengthening mechanisms operating in binary Fe-Al based ferritic low-density steels with different Al contents (5, 6, 6.8 and 9 wt%), focusing on Fe-6.8Al; combines microstructural characterization (Mössbauer spectroscopy, SAXS, TEM, XRD) with constitutive modelling of individual strengthening contributions (grain size, dislocations, ordered phase, solid solution and lattice friction) for cold-rolled and annealed conditions.
paper.title: Strengthening mechanisms in Fe-Al based ferritic low-density steels

unmapped_findings: Pure α-Fe foil was used only as a calibration/reference standard for Mössbauer spectroscopy (velocity calibration and comparison with pure Fe), not as a studied low-density steel.

The nano-sized ordered phase was identified as Fe3Al with DO3 structure, and a possible B2 (FeAl) ordered phase was also indicated; ordered phase size ranged from 2.5 to 3.75 nm and increased with Al content.

The paper cites literature comparison alloys (e.g., Fe-30.5Mn-8.0Al-1.2C, Fe-9Al-28Mn-1.8C, Fe-3.5Mn-2.9Si-0.3C, Fe-18Ni-0.001C, Al-Mg-Sc alloy, and a 0.4 wt% C-steel) that are used as references for strengthening models and are not studied experimentally here.
Measured compositions (by WDS/EPMA) and density measurements (Archimedes principle) for the alloys are reported in Ref. [15] rather than in this paper.
The lattice frictional stress was taken as 41 MPa (from a 0.4 wt% C-steel, Speich and Swann [46]) due to unavailability of literature data for Fe-Al alloys.
